1	# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow
2	
3	Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.
4	
5	This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Functional requirements
10	
11	### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
12	Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).
13	
14	**Acceptance criteria:**
15	- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
16	- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.
17	
18	### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
19	Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.
20	
21	**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.
22	
23	### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
24	Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.
25	
26	**Acceptance criteria:**
27	- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
28	- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).
29	
30	### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
31	Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.
32	
33	**Acceptance criteria:**
34	- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
35	- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).
36	
37	### RF05 — Personal summary export
38	Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**
39	
40	**Acceptance criteria:**
41	- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
42	- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.
43	
44	### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
45	Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).
46	
47	**Acceptance criteria:**
48	- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
49	- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
50	- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
51	- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
52	- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.
53	
54	### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
55	A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.
56	
57	**Acceptance criteria:**
58	- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
59	- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
60	- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.
61	
62	### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
63	A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**
64	
65	**Acceptance criteria:**
66	- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
67	- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
68	- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.
69	
70	### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
71	An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**
72	
73	**Acceptance criteria:**
74	- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
75	- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
76	- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.
77	
78	### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
79	A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.

# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.

This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.

---

## 1. Functional requirements

### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.

### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.

**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.

### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).

### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).

### RF05 — Personal summary export
Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.

### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.

### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.

### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.

### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.

dev_dependencies:

    sdk: flutter

  # The "flutter_lints" package below contains a set of recommended lints to

  # --- Stack Pins (architecture spine) ---
  freezed: ^4.0.3
  json_serializable: ^6.15.2
  build_runner: any
  mocktail: ^1.0.5

  # Story 3.1 — `registerEntriesFeature()`'s `Hive.initFlutter()` is the
  # app's first use of `path_provider` (transitively, via
  # `hive_ce_flutter`). No device/simulator exists yet (AGENTS.md), so
  # `bootstrap_integration_test.dart`/`main_test.dart` fake this plugin's
  # platform-interface instance directly, same "fake the native platform
  # channel" pattern they already use for `flutter_secure_storage`.
  path_provider_platform_interface: ^2.1.3

# For information on the generic Dart part of this file, see the
# following page: https://dart.dev/tools/pub/pubspec

# The following section is specific to Flutter packages.
flutter:

  # .env is never committed (gitignored) — each environment/developer
  # supplies their own, holding exactly FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL and
  # SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, loaded via flutter_dotenv (never hardcoded).
  assets:
    - .env

  # The following line ensures that the Material Icons font is
  # included with your application, so that you can use the icons in
  # the material Icons class.
  uses-material-design: true

  # To add assets to your application, add an assets section, like this:
  # assets:
  #   - images/a_dot_burr.jpeg
  #   - images/a_dot_ham.jpeg

  # An image asset can refer to one or more resolution-specific "variants", see
  # https://flutter.dev/to/resolution-aware-images

  # For details regarding adding assets from package dependencies, see
  # https://flutter.dev/to/asset-from-package

  # Story 1.2 — the three prototype type families (prototype-extract.md §3),
  # bundled as static assets (never `google_fonts`, which fetches at
  # runtime) so widget tests stay deterministic with no device/network.
  # Fraunces and Karla ship from Google Fonts as variable fonts (one file,
  # `wght` axis) — the same asset is listed once per weight actually used
  # by a `design_tokens.dart` typography token, which is the documented
  # pattern for selecting a named instance via `TextStyle.fontWeight`.
  fonts:
    - family: Fraunces
      fonts:
        - asset: assets/fonts/Fraunces-Variable.ttf
          weight: 600
    - family: Karla
      fonts:
        - asset: assets/fonts/Karla-Variable.ttf
          weight: 400
        - asset: assets/fonts/Karla-Variable.ttf
          weight: 500
        - asset: assets/fonts/Karla-Variable.ttf
          weight: 700
    - family: IBMPlexMono
      fonts:
        - asset: assets/fonts/IBMPlexMono-Medium.ttf
          weight: 500

1	---
2	title: 'Story 3.1: Text Entry Capture & Insertion Modal Shell'
3	type: 'feature'
4	created: '2026-11-04'
5	status: 'done'
6	review_loop_iteration: 0
7	context: []
8	baseline_commit: '12cdeaa93f773d1e68061196f04bb89627cdc849'
9	---
10	
11	<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">
12	
13	## Intent
14	
15	**Problem:** There is no way to capture a journal Entry yet — `features/entries/` and `features/capture/` are empty scaffolds, and the Home/Chat screen has no "+" entry point.
16	
17	**Approach:** Stand up `features/entries/` (Entry entity, `EntriesRepository.create` port, entries Hive box) and `features/capture/` (Insertion Modal bottom sheet with 3 tabs), and add a minimal "+" control to the Home/Chat placeholder that opens it. Only the Texto tab is functional this story.
18	
19	## Boundaries & Constraints
20	
21	**Always:**
22	- `features/entries/domain` owns `Entry` (plain class, no freezed — mirrors `AuthenticatedUser`), `EntrySource` enum (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`), and `EntriesRepository` (abstract, one method: `create`). `features/capture/` imports only `entries/domain`, never `entries/data` or `entries/presentation` (RNF06).
23	- `EntriesRepository.create` → `Either<Failure, Entry>`, posts to `entries-create` via the shared `ApiClient.post`, source=`manual` for this story. On success, write the entry through to the `entries` Hive box (`Box<Map>`, keyed by id) — first use of `hive_ce` in the app.
24	- Insertion Modal: `showModalBottomSheet(isScrollControlled: true, barrierColor: DesignTokens.colorScrimHeavy)`, `radiusLg` top corners, `elevation2`, new `DesignTokens.durationSheetUp` (200ms) entrance, skipped under Reduce Motion. 3 equal-width tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto); only the active tab fills `colorPrimary`. Close "x" always present. Opens on Texto, all 3 tabs idle/empty.
25	- Texto tab: text field + Salvar. Salvar fires `POST /entries`; success closes the modal; failure (including offline, via the existing `Failure.networkOffline`) shows `Failure.message` inline and re-enables Salvar — no auto-retry, reuse `Failure.fromCode`/`retryable` as-is.
26	- "+" control on `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen`: always tappable, opens the modal. No proactive offline detection or banner in this story (deferred — see Spec Change Log / `deferred-work.md`); an offline save attempt surfaces the same way any other failed save does.
27	- 44pt tap targets, Dynamic Type with no truncation, announced labels for every state change (no color-only signal).
28	
29	**Ask First:** none identified.
30	
31	**Never:**
32	- Implement Áudio/Foto tab capture logic (render idle/empty only — Stories 3.2/3.3).
33	- Implement the full cross-tab cancel-safety rule (Story 3.4) — this story only needs the trivial case: the text tab never calls `create` except on explicit Salvar.
34	- Build the full chat composer (text field + send icon) — RF04's scope. Add only the "+" tap target.
35	- Add a connectivity service, offline banner, or any proactive offline-disabling of "+" — deferred (see `deferred-work.md`); no existing pattern to reuse, and the prototype doesn't represent this state.
36	- Add `GET /entries`, listing, search, or any `Entry` fields beyond `{id, content, source, chatMessageId, occurredAt, serverRevision, createdAt, updatedAt}` (tags/piiStatus/embeddingStatus belong to later epics).
37	- Use the shared `Resource<T>` type for capture's state — capture defines its own sealed state class.
38	
39	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
40	
41	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
42	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
43	| Happy path save | Texto tab, non-empty text, tap Salvar | `POST /entries` (`source: manual`) fires; on success modal closes, returns to Home | N/A |
44	| Modal open resets | "+" tapped | Opens on Texto; all 3 tabs idle/empty regardless of prior session | N/A |
45	| Save fails (incl. offline) | Salvar tapped, backend call returns a mapped error code (e.g. `NETWORK_OFFLINE`) | Inline message from `Failure.message`; Salvar re-enabled; modal stays open | `Failure.fromCode`, no auto-retry |
46	| Cancel before save | "x" tapped or user leaves with unsaved text | Modal closes/resets; no `POST /entries` fires | N/A |
47	
48	</frozen-after-approval>
49	
50	## Code Map
51	
52	- `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart:76-130` (`HomeChatPlaceholderScreen`) — add the "+" entry point here; body is currently a pure placeholder (RF04 not built), no composer exists.
53	- `lib/core/design_tokens.dart:85` (`colorScrimHeavy`, already reserved for "a later story's insertion modal"), `:199` (`radiusLg`), `:218` (`elevation2`) — reuse as-is; add `durationSheetUp` near these, no `Duration`/motion token exists yet.
54	- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart:67-83` (`Failure.fromCode`) — reuse unchanged; already generic, no new mapping needed.
55	- `lib/core/network/api_client.dart:52-62` (`post`) — call via the new `EntriesRemoteDataSource`.
56	- `lib/core/network/header_interceptor.dart:20-24` (`anonKeyOnlyFunctions`) — `entries-create` is not in that set, so it auto-gets the user bearer token; no changes needed.
57	- `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart:26-84` (`setupCoreDependencies`) — add `Hive.initFlutter()` + `registerEntriesFeature()` + `registerCaptureFeature()`, after the existing `registerAccountFeature()` call.
58	- `lib/features/account/account_injection.dart`, `account_remote_data_source.dart`, `account_settings_dto.dart`, `account_settings_repository_impl.dart`, `account_settings_cubit.dart` — structural patterns to mirror (DI registration, `ApiClient` datasource, `@JsonSerializable` DTO, repository impl, cubit calling repository directly — no use-case layer exists in this codebase).
59	- `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/authenticated_user.dart` — plain-class entity pattern (no freezed) to mirror for `Entry`.
60	- `lib/features/entries/{data,domain,presentation}/.gitkeep`, `lib/features/capture/{data,domain,presentation}/.gitkeep` — empty scaffolds to fill.
61	- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:327-449` — `entries-create` request/response schema.
62	- `pubspec.yaml:42-43` — `hive_ce`/`hive_ce_flutter` already a dependency, unused until now.
63	- `test/features/account/**` — test directory layout to mirror under `test/features/entries/` and `test/features/capture/`.
64	
65	## Tasks & Acceptance
66	
67	**Execution:**
68	- [x] `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` -- add `durationSheetUp = Duration(milliseconds: 200)` -- no entrance-animation token exists yet (RNF08).
69	- [x] `lib/features/entries/domain/entities/entry.dart` (new) -- `Entry` class + `EntrySource` enum -- mirrors `AuthenticatedUser`.
70	- [x] `lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` (new) -- abstract `EntriesRepository.create(...)` → `Future<Either<Failure, Entry>>` -- the port later epics extend.
71	- [x] `lib/features/entries/data/models/entry_dto.dart` (+ generated `.g.dart`) -- `@JsonSerializable()` mirroring the response `data` object.
72	- [x] `lib/features/entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` (new) -- posts to `entries-create` via `ApiClient.post`, decodes `EntryDto`.
73	- [x] `lib/features/entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart` (new) -- implements `create`; on success writes to the `entries` Hive box keyed by id; maps `EntryDto` → `Entry`.
74	- [x] `lib/features/entries/entries_injection.dart` (new) -- registers datasource/repository, opens/registers the `entries` Hive box.
75	- [x] `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart` -- wire `Hive.initFlutter()` + `registerEntriesFeature()` + `registerCaptureFeature()`.
76	- [x] `lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/text_entry_cubit.dart` (new) -- own sealed state (active tab, text, saving/error); calls `EntriesRepository.create` directly on Salvar.
77	- [x] `lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart` (new) -- 3-tab bottom sheet; Texto functional, Áudio/Foto idle placeholders.
78	- [x] `lib/features/capture/capture_injection.dart` (new) -- registers `TextEntryCubit`.
79	- [x] `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart` -- add the always-tappable "+" control to `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen` that opens `InsertionModal`.
80	- [x] Unit/widget tests under `test/features/entries/`, `test/features/capture/` covering the I/O matrix above.
81	
82	**Acceptance Criteria:**

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** There is no way to capture a journal Entry yet — `features/entries/` and `features/capture/` are empty scaffolds, and the Home/Chat screen has no "+" entry point.

**Approach:** Stand up `features/entries/` (Entry entity, `EntriesRepository.create` port, entries Hive box) and `features/capture/` (Insertion Modal bottom sheet with 3 tabs), and add a minimal "+" control to the Home/Chat placeholder that opens it. Only the Texto tab is functional this story.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `features/entries/domain` owns `Entry` (plain class, no freezed — mirrors `AuthenticatedUser`), `EntrySource` enum (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`), and `EntriesRepository` (abstract, one method: `create`). `features/capture/` imports only `entries/domain`, never `entries/data` or `entries/presentation` (RNF06).
- `EntriesRepository.create` → `Either<Failure, Entry>`, posts to `entries-create` via the shared `ApiClient.post`, source=`manual` for this story. On success, write the entry through to the `entries` Hive box (`Box<Map>`, keyed by id) — first use of `hive_ce` in the app.
- Insertion Modal: `showModalBottomSheet(isScrollControlled: true, barrierColor: DesignTokens.colorScrimHeavy)`, `radiusLg` top corners, `elevation2`, new `DesignTokens.durationSheetUp` (200ms) entrance, skipped under Reduce Motion. 3 equal-width tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto); only the active tab fills `colorPrimary`. Close "x" always present. Opens on Texto, all 3 tabs idle/empty.
- Texto tab: text field + Salvar. Salvar fires `POST /entries`; success closes the modal; failure (including offline, via the existing `Failure.networkOffline`) shows `Failure.message` inline and re-enables Salvar — no auto-retry, reuse `Failure.fromCode`/`retryable` as-is.
- "+" control on `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen`: always tappable, opens the modal. No proactive offline detection or banner in this story (deferred — see Spec Change Log / `deferred-work.md`); an offline save attempt surfaces the same way any other failed save does.
- 44pt tap targets, Dynamic Type with no truncation, announced labels for every state change (no color-only signal).

**Ask First:** none identified.

**Never:**
- Implement Áudio/Foto tab capture logic (render idle/empty only — Stories 3.2/3.3).
- Implement the full cross-tab cancel-safety rule (Story 3.4) — this story only needs the trivial case: the text tab never calls `create` except on explicit Salvar.
- Build the full chat composer (text field + send icon) — RF04's scope. Add only the "+" tap target.
- Add a connectivity service, offline banner, or any proactive offline-disabling of "+" — deferred (see `deferred-work.md`); no existing pattern to reuse, and the prototype doesn't represent this state.
- Add `GET /entries`, listing, search, or any `Entry` fields beyond `{id, content, source, chatMessageId, occurredAt, serverRevision, createdAt, updatedAt}` (tags/piiStatus/embeddingStatus belong to later epics).
- Use the shared `Resource<T>` type for capture's state — capture defines its own sealed state class.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Happy path save | Texto tab, non-empty text, tap Salvar | `POST /entries` (`source: manual`) fires; on success modal closes, returns to Home | N/A |
| Modal open resets | "+" tapped | Opens on Texto; all 3 tabs idle/empty regardless of prior session | N/A |
| Save fails (incl. offline) | Salvar tapped, backend call returns a mapped error code (e.g. `NETWORK_OFFLINE`) | Inline message from `Failure.message`; Salvar re-enabled; modal stays open | `Failure.fromCode`, no auto-retry |
| Cancel before save | "x" tapped or user leaves with unsaved text | Modal closes/resets; no `POST /entries` fires | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

5	/// AD-3 — the one closed `Failure` hierarchy, exactly 14 subtypes: the 13
6	/// codes from `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md` plus the local-only
7	/// `malformedResponse` (client-side parse failure, never sent by the
8	/// backend). Never redefined or subset per feature; every repository method
9	/// returns `Either<Failure, T>` built from this type (RNF09).
10	///
11	/// `retryable` is derived here, once, from the 6 server `retryable:true`
12	/// codes (AD-4) — no other file re-decides which codes retry.
13	@freezed
14	sealed class Failure with _$Failure {
15	  const factory Failure.authExpired({required String message}) = AuthExpired;
16	  const factory Failure.authInvalid({required String message}) = AuthInvalid;
17	  const factory Failure.networkTimeout({required String message}) =
18	      NetworkTimeout;
19	  const factory Failure.networkOffline({required String message}) =
20	      NetworkOffline;
21	  const factory Failure.validation({required String message}) = Validation;
22	  const factory Failure.piiCheckFailed({required String message}) =
23	      PiiCheckFailed;
24	  const factory Failure.embeddingFailed({required String message}) =
25	      EmbeddingFailed;
26	  const factory Failure.aiGenerationTimeout({required String message}) =
27	      AiGenerationTimeout;
28	  const factory Failure.notFound({required String message}) = NotFound;
29	  const factory Failure.rateLimited({required String message}) = RateLimited;
30	  const factory Failure.exportEmptyPeriod({required String message}) =
31	      ExportEmptyPeriod;
32	  const factory Failure.payloadTooLarge({required String message}) =
33	      PayloadTooLarge;
34	  const factory Failure.ocrNoText({required String message}) = OcrNoText;
35	
36	  /// Local-only — the client's own parse-failure detection. `retryable` is
37	  /// hardcoded `false` for this subtype (AD-3).
38	  const factory Failure.malformedResponse({required String message}) =
39	      MalformedResponse;
40	
41	  const Failure._();
42	
43	  /// The 6 server `retryable:true` codes (AD-4). Every other code —
44	  /// including the local `malformedResponse` — is `false`.
45	  bool get retryable => switch (this) {
46	        NetworkTimeout() => true,
47	        NetworkOffline() => true,
48	        PiiCheckFailed() => true,
49	        EmbeddingFailed() => true,
50	        AiGenerationTimeout() => true,

53	        AuthInvalid() ||
54	        Validation() ||

70	        'NETWORK_TIMEOUT' => Failure.networkTimeout(message: message),

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.text: The zone interaction between `runAsync` and widget-pumping APIs (tap/pump) is exactly the kind of fragile territory Flutter's test docs warn against — mixing real I/O with simulated UI interaction isn't reliable here. This codebase's own convention already resolves this split cleanly: UI-driven tests always use a fake repository (already done thoroughly in `insertion_modal_test.dart`), and real-pipeline tests are plain `test()` functions that drive the real objects directly, no widget pumping involved. I'll rewrite this test to resolve the real, DI-wired `TextEntryCubit` — the exact instance the "+" button gets — and drive it directly through its public API (`updateText`/`save()`), which avoids the zone problem entirely since there's no tap/pump involved.
Now let's rewrite the whole file with the plain-`test()` approach, driving the real resolved cubit directly.

## Summary

I generated a new E2E test suite for the most recently completed story (3.1 — text entry capture & insertion modal shell), since it's the feature with uncommitted/recent changes and no existing test exercises the full real stack together.

**File added:** [test/features/capture/capture_flow_e2e_test.dart](test/features/capture/capture_flow_e2e_test.dart)

This fills a real gap: existing tests for this story each isolate one layer (`insertion_modal_test.dart` uses a fake repository, `entries_repository_impl_integration_test.dart` mocks the datasource, `bootstrap_integration_test.dart` only checks DI resolves without exercising a save). Nothing drove the actual production object graph through a full create flow.

The new suite resolves the real `TextEntryCubit` via `sl<TextEntryCubit>()` — the exact instance the "+" FAB gets — wired to the real `EntriesRepositoryImpl` → `EntriesRemoteDataSource` → `ApiClient`/`Dio` (both real interceptors) → a real Hive box. Only the HTTP transport and native plugins (secure storage, path_provider) are faked, matching this repo's existing "no device/CI" testing convention (AGENTS.md).

Two cases, matching the skill's "happy path + 1-2 errors" guidance:
- **Happy path**: real POST to `entries-create` with correct URL/headers/body → `TextEntrySaved` → entry actually persisted in the real Hive box.
- **Failure path**: non-retryable `VALIDATION_ERROR` → `TextEntryError` with `Failure.message` verbatim, exactly one request (no retry), nothing written to Hive.

One worth flagging: I initially drove this through `tester.tap()`/`pumpAndSettle()` on the real widget, which deadlocked — real async I/O (Dio, Hive disk writes) doesn't reliably resolve under Flutter's fake-async test clock, and wrapping it in `tester.runAsync()` broke platform-channel mocking instead of fixing it. I dropped the widget-tap approach and drove the cubit's public API (`updateText`/`save()`) directly in a plain `test()`, which is also exactly how the three existing "integration" tests in this repo already avoid the same pitfall.

`fvm flutter analyze` (whole project) and `fvm flutter test` (full suite, 404 tests) both pass clean.
